title: Revised Framework Stages 2–4
review_status: Team working draft. Not externally reviewed. The links from Stage 2 rows to ECAM stages and emission sources were added by the ChatWater build and await team review.
links_note: Added by ChatWater to connect framework rows to ECAM stages, emission sources and existing Stage 2 rules. Awaiting team review. They guide questions only; they do not create or change action rules.

stage2.group_title: Water supply: emission outputs and potential actions
questions: Is energy use unusually high per unit of water abstracted?
Have falling groundwater levels, drought, changing river levels, or increased pumping head increased energy demand?
Are pumps operating efficiently?
actions: solar pumping where technically and financially suitable

stage2.group_title: Water supply: emission outputs and potential actions
questions: Are diesel or petrol engines used for routine pumping or during grid outages?
How much fuel is consumed?
Are outages or climate hazards increasing dependence on backup engines?
actions: assess solar-plus-storage or other suitable alternatives
establish fuel reserves and backup-power protocols for critical assets

stage2.group_title: Water supply: emission outputs and potential actions
questions: Which treatment processes consume the most electricity?
Does raw-water quality deteriorate during floods, droughts, or algal blooms, requiring more intensive treatment?
Is equipment operating efficiently?
actions: Optimize treatment operations and chemical dosing
protect critical treatment equipment from flooding

stage2.group_title: Water supply: emission outputs and potential actions
questions: Is fuel used for backup power, pumping, or other treatment operations?
Are extreme weather events causing more frequent generator use?
actions: prioritize backup supply for essential treatment processes

stage2.group_title: Water supply: emission outputs and potential actions
questions: Which pumping stations have the highest energy intensity?
Are leakage, pressure-management problems, topography, or excessive pumping head increasing energy demand?
Are droughts or intermittent supply changing operating patterns?
actions: storage and gravity-fed distribution where feasible
renewable power at suitable pumping stations

stage2.group_title: Water supply: emission outputs and potential actions
questions: Are engines used to maintain pressure or supply during outages?
Which distribution zones are most affected by power interruptions, flooding, or extreme heat?
actions: emergency distribution plans and critical-spares management

stage2.group_title: Sanitation: emission outputs and potential actions
questions: Which lift stations or collection assets consume the most energy?
Is infiltration of stormwater or groundwater increasing the volume pumped?
Are pumps frequently clogged or overloaded?
actions: backup power for critical pumping assets

stage2.group_title: Sanitation: emission outputs and potential actions
questions: Are fuel engines used for wastewater pumping or backup power?
Do floods, power failures, or access problems increase their use?

stage2.group_title: Sanitation: emission outputs and potential actions
questions: Are long retention times, stagnant flows, warm conditions, or anaerobic zones contributing to methane generation?
Are sewer blockages or flooding creating operational problems?
actions: improve flow management and hotspot monitoring
assess methane mitigation options where feasible. Avoid assuming that increasing aeration or flow is automatically the best solution

stage2.group_title: Sanitation: emission outputs and potential actions
stage2.output: Collection — untreated wastewater discharge, where included in the ECAM inventory
questions: Is wastewater bypassing treatment or being discharged untreated?
Are heavy rainfall, sewer overflows, or inadequate capacity contributing?
Which communities and receiving waters are most exposed?
actions: expand treatment coverage and protect receiving waters

stage2.group_title: Sanitation: emission outputs and potential actions
questions: Which processes—especially aeration, pumping, mixing, and sludge handling—use the most energy?
Does wet-weather inflow, changing wastewater strength, or poor equipment performance increase demand?
actions: assess renewable electricity and resilient power supplies

stage2.group_title: Sanitation: emission outputs and potential actions
questions: How much fuel is used by generators and other treatment-plant engines?
Are power interruptions compromising treatment continuity?
actions: assess hybrid or renewable backup systems

stage2.group_title: Sanitation: emission outputs and potential actions
questions: Which treatment configurations and operating conditions contribute to emissions?
Are temperature, loading, aeration, or nitrogen-removal conditions influencing emissions?
Is treatment performance deteriorating during extreme weather?
actions: Optimize process operation and aeration control
assess methane capture or treatment-process modifications where appropriate

stage2.group_title: Sanitation: emission outputs and potential actions
questions: Is biogas generated, used for energy, flared, sold, or lost through leakage?
Is anaerobic digestion operating reliably?
Are flood, heat, or power risks affecting gas handling?
actions: improve gas collection and safety systems
evaluate combined heat and power or direct energy recovery
maintain appropriate flaring as a safety measure when recovery is unavailable

stage2.group_title: Sanitation: emission outputs and potential actions
questions: Is the effluent meeting applicable quality requirements?
Are receiving waters vulnerable to low flows, high temperatures, flooding, or reduced dilution?
Are discharge conditions worsening during extreme events?
actions: Improve process control and effluent monitoring
add or optimize treatment where justified
consider safe reuse where appropriate and permitted

stage2.group_title: Sanitation: emission outputs and potential actions
stage2.output: Onsite sanitation — process emissions and biogas, where included
questions: Which containment or decentralized treatment systems contribute to emissions?
Are methane generation, leakage, emptying practices, or faecal-sludge treatment and disposal creating environmental risks?
Are floods or groundwater changes threatening containment integrity?
actions: protect vulnerable sanitation infrastructure from flooding and groundwater impacts

stage2.group_title: Water supply indicators
stage2.output: Energy consumption per unit of water abstracted, treated, or distributed
questions: Which stage has the highest energy intensity?
Is performance worsening over time?
Is the difference explained by operating conditions or avoidable inefficiency?

stage2.group_title: Water supply indicators
stage2.output: Energy consumption per unit of pumped water
questions: Are pumps operating near their design conditions?
Are head requirements, flow rates, or pump efficiency driving excessive energy consumption?

stage2.group_title: Water supply indicators
questions: Does performance remain poor after accounting for pump head, making the system more comparable with other installations?

stage2.group_title: Water supply indicators
questions: Is measured pump efficiency low?
Are worn components, poor motor performance, or incorrect sizing contributing?

stage2.group_title: Water supply indicators
stage2.output: Unit head loss and hydraulic performance
questions: Are friction losses, pipe restrictions, undersized pipes, or deteriorating infrastructure increasing pumping requirements?

stage2.group_title: Water supply indicators
stage2.output: Water losses and distribution performance, where available in the assessment
questions: Are leaks, pressure problems, or intermittent supply contributing to energy waste or service disruption?

stage2.group_title: Water supply indicators
stage2.output: Water treatment performance and service coverage
questions: Is treatment capacity adequate during source-water deterioration or extreme rainfall?
Is the utility providing reliable, safe water to its intended population?

stage2.group_title: Sanitation indicators
stage2.output: Energy consumption per unit of wastewater collected or treated
questions: Are pumping requirements, infiltration, equipment efficiency, or treatment processes driving high energy demand?

stage2.group_title: Sanitation indicators
stage2.output: Electromechanical efficiency and standardized pumping energy
questions: Are wastewater pumps inefficient, clogged, overloaded, or operating under unfavorable hydraulic conditions?

stage2.group_title: Sanitation indicators
questions: Are treatment processes meeting applicable performance requirements under normal and extreme weather conditions?

stage2.group_title: Sanitation indicators
stage2.output: Population connected to wastewater collection and treatment
questions: Which areas lack adequate sanitation services?
Are low-income or flood-prone communities disproportionately underserved?
actions: decentralized or nature-based treatment where suitable

stage2.group_title: Sanitation indicators
stage2.output: Wastewater generated but not collected or treated
questions: Is untreated wastewater entering drains, watercourses, or the environment?
Could rainfall overwhelm the system?

stage2.group_title: Sanitation indicators
questions: Is sludge safely removed, transported, treated, and disposed of or reused?
Are flooding or access disruptions affecting sludge management?

stage2.group_title: Sanitation indicators
questions: Is biogas being captured and used effectively?
Are leakage, flaring, or unreliable equipment reducing the benefits?

stage2.group_title: Sanitation indicators
stage2.output: Onsite sanitation and faecal-sludge service performance
questions: Are containment systems vulnerable to flooding or groundwater intrusion?
Are emptying and treatment services adequate and safe?

stage3.title: Establish the baseline
questions: What is the current level of emissions, energy consumption or service disruption?
What climate hazards affect the project location?
What baseline data are available, and what additional assessments are required?
How will the utility measure improvement against the baseline?

stage3.title: Identify project activities
stage3.description: Translate the selected action into work packages
questions: What activities are required to implement the selected action?
What technical investigations, designs, permits or approvals are needed?
What are the main implementation milestones?
What must be completed before implementation can begin?

stage3.title: Assess implementation risks
stage3.description: Delivery risks and resilience under future conditions

cost_components: Estimated capital expenditure (CAPEX) required to implement the project
Costs associated with feasibility studies, engineering design, procurement, installation, training and monitoring
Contingency allowances, taxes, inflation and price escalation included
Expected project lifetime and the likely timing of major replacement costs
stage4.note: The framework lists "Funding gap" and "Source of funding" without further detail; ChatWater does not compute either.
